key_insight: Adapted DINOv2 generalised better than task-specific models on every external dataset, while task-specific models remained competitive within the training distribution when data were abundant.
clinical_relevance: Foundation-model adaptation may improve segmentation across clinical sites, although small-lesion misses and less precise boundaries warrant careful validation.
method: Adapted DINOv2 using strategies from bias-only tuning to full fine-tuning.
Compared against U-Nets and ResU-Nets trained from scratch.
Evaluated colonoscopy, breast ultrasound and dermoscopy segmentation.
evidence_signal: Testing included held-out source data and independent datasets from other institutions; only a small fraction of DINOv2 required adaptation, with capacity needs varying by imaging domain.
watch_item: A widely used polyp test set contained images duplicated from another benchmark, underscoring the need to check evaluation-set independence.
paper_title: Medical Image Segmentation: Foundation Model Adaptation versus Task-Specific Training
